title: The Last Hollow Again
premise: Wendell Oyelaran has spent thirty years mapping realms he can never enter, hiding in the Hollow—a valley where magic dies at the borders—because his blood carries a covenant that once ended an ancient war. When a mute child arrives speaking a pre-kingdom tongue, Wendell realizes the war's losing side has found him, and the child is both a key and a target. Pursued by the Ashen Court's hunters, Wendell must cross the unmapped lands he has only ever drawn, discovering that the maps were never records but bindings—and that his own hand helped write them. In the end, Wendell chooses to unbind the covenant, surrendering the valley's protection and his own memories of belonging, so the child can carry a new, freer magic into the world.
about_author: Z. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent a decade charting coastlines before turning to cartography of imaginary places. They live at the edge of a forest they refuse to map, writing stories about people who draw borders and the things that cross them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He finishes a map of a realm he'll never see, burning the draft as ritual requires, while the valley's elders remind him why magic cannot follow anyone inside. The beat is quiet dread: routine as armor, and the first hairline crack in it when he notices the border stones have shifted overnight.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A girl of perhaps eight appears in a snowstorm, speaking a language older than any kingdom—yet Wendell understands her, which terrifies him more than her arrival. The emotional beat is reluctant tenderness colliding with self-preservation as he hides her from the valley's watchmen.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with the child (named Sef) communicating through drawings on his maps. Her sketches match places from Wendell's oldest, forbidden folio—the one he inherited from his mother. The beat is recognition and grief: his past was never buried, only filed away.

chapters.title: The Ashen Court Wakes
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Veyra, a hunter of the Ashen Court, tracking a 'leak' in the covenant across the deadlands. Through her we learn the war never ended—it was paused, and the pause is failing. The beat is cold menace sharpened by her own doubt about what she serves.

chapters.title: Borders Are Promises
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The valley council discovers Sef and demands her expulsion; Wendell lies for the first time in thirty years. His mentor, Ilsa, reveals she has always known what Wendell's blood is. The beat is betrayal and grace intertwined—belonging offered at the cost of truth.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Road
chapters.summary: Wendell flees with Sef into the wilds beyond the valley, using his own maps to navigate—but the terrain no longer matches them, because Sef's presence rewrites reality. The beat is disorientation becoming wonder: the cartographer lost in a world that refuses to hold still.

chapters.title: Veyra's Ledger
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. She closes in, interrogating a village that sheltered them, and uncovers evidence that the Court plans to use Sef not to end the war but to restart it on favorable terms. The beat is a hunter's crisis of faith; she begins keeping a second, private ledger.

chapters.title: The Binding Room
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the ruined archive where the covenant was written, he learns the terrible truth: his ancestors didn't end the war—they bound all magic to a price paid by bloodlines like his, and his mother died feeding it. The beat is fury and vertigo; survival itself becomes the thing to forgive.

chapters.title: Where the War Waits
chapters.summary: Climax. Veyra corners them at the archive as the Court's vanguard arrives; Sef, terrified, unleashes the old language and nearly reignites the war. Wendell offers the alternative: unbinding the covenant with his own blood and memory. The beat is sacrifice chosen freely, Veyra turning her blade against her own Court.

chapters.title: A Map With No Edges
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, fragmented—he remembers less each day, but the valley opens its borders and magic returns gently, not violently. Sef stays with Ilsa; Veyra becomes the new covenant's first witness. The final beat is bittersweet belonging: Wendell no longer knows why he stayed, only that he is home.
